citation.title: Deep learning accelerated topology optimization of linear and nonlinear structures
citation.authors: Diab W. Abueidda, Seid Koric, Nahil A. Sobh

included.physics: linear elasticity, stress and neo-Hookean hyperelasticity

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: After offline training, the CNN predicts topology designs with negligible per-query computation instead of running an iterative classical optimizer.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Sections 3.1 and 5 give classical generation times but no numeric CNN inference time, so no ratio can be calculated.
claim.alternatives: Section 3.1 reports classical runs of roughly 25 minutes for linear and 90 minutes for nonlinear cases on a Core i5 computer; conclusion claims instant laptop inference.

baseline.classical_method: Section 2: SIMP with MMA; linear and nonlinear examples generated with ABAQUS/TOSCA, stress-constrained examples with in-house MATLAB MMA code
baseline.implementation: Section 2: general-purpose commercial ABAQUS/TOSCA for linear/nonlinear cases; in-house MATLAB for stress-constrained case
baseline.hardware_classical: Section 3.1: iForge Intel Skylake nodes, 40 cores and 192 GB RAM, up to ten simultaneous cases; also Core i5 vPro computer for single-run times
baseline.hardware_ml: Section 5: iForge node with one NVIDIA V100 32 GB GPU for training; conclusion mentions laptop inference without hardware specification
baseline.problem_size: Section 3.1: 32 x 32 elements linear, 50 x 50 nonlinear; section 3.2: 50 x 50 stress-constrained
baseline.classical_time: Section 3.1: roughly 25 minutes linear and 90 minutes nonlinear per optimization on Core i5 vPro
baseline.ml_time: Abstract and conclusion: negligible or instant inference; no number stated
baseline.training_time: Section 5, Fig. 7: 1.25 hours linear and 1.5 hours nonlinear on one V100 GPU; linear 12.5 hours on CPU-only Skylake node
baseline.data_generation_cost: Section 3.1, Fig. 4: 15,000 linear pairs at average 0.31 minutes per pair; 18,000 nonlinear pairs at 3.2 minutes per pair with ten parallel optimizations; section 3.2: 20,000 stress-constrained pairs, time not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Section 5: Dice similarity coefficient and mean squared error comparing thresholded output images to classical designs
baseline.quality_gap: Section 5: mean test Dice coefficient 0.958 linear, 0.964 nonlinear, 0.984 stress-constrained; physical objective gap not stated

R1.evidence: Abstract and section 5: negligible CNN inference is contrasted with iterative classical optimization, but output quality is evaluated by image overlap without matched compliance, stress or physical volume at the timed result.

R2.evidence: Section 2: linear and nonlinear labels are produced with general-purpose ABAQUS/TOSCA; no same-hardware comparison with an efficient sparse or multigrid classical implementation is available.

R3.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 5 state generation rate and training time for linear and nonlinear cases, but section 3.2 and section 5 omit the corresponding costs for the stress-constrained model; no break-even number is given.

R4.evidence: Section 5, Figs. 10-13: returned topologies are compared with classical output mainly through Dice overlap and selected images; no FE recomputation of physical quality or constraint/failure rates for returned designs is shown.

reporting.n_test_cases: Sections 3 and 5: 10% test split of 15,000 linear, 18,000 nonlinear, and 20,000 stress-constrained generated examples

notes: The numeric 10-fold comparison in section 5 concerns GPU versus CPU training of the same CNN, not CNN versus classical topology optimization; it is not the primary outcome. Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.01896v4
